claims.evidence: Photo 2 control panel clearly reads 'SHARP AR-9201', not AR-M201

claims.claim: Fairly used, fully functional, and ready to [use]
claims.evidence: No power-on, print, or copy test shown in any photo
No counter/display screenshot showing page count

claims.claim: New drum and toner just fitted
claims.evidence: No photo of opened toner/drum compartment or new part packaging
No video or test print showing paper path/feed in action

risks.risk: Unit may not power on or may have internal faults
risks.proof: Video of power-on, control panel lighting up, and a test copy being produced

risks.risk: Actual page count could be much higher than claimed
risks.proof: Clear photo/screenshot of the internal page counter on the control panel display

risks.risk: Drum/toner may be old or near end-of-life despite claim
risks.proof: Photo of open toner/drum unit showing new part labels or fill level
risks.if_unproven: priced as original/worn consumables needing replacement

risks.risk: Model identity confusion (seller says AR-M201, panel reads AR-9201) could affect true specs and part compatibility
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rating/model plate (usually on rear or inside panel) confirming exact model
risks.if_unproven: priced per witness-confirmed model AR-9201 only

risks.risk: Missing trays, cables, or feeder parts not visible
risks.proof: Full-view photos of all sides, rear ports, power cable, and paper trays

risks.risk: Hidden physical/internal damage (wiring, rollers, feeder mechanism)
risks.proof: Photos/video of document feeder opened and internal rollers

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the model/rating plate (not just control panel)
Video of power-on sequence and a live test copy/print
Screenshot or photo of the internal page counter
Photo of open toner and drum compartment showing part condition
Photos of all sides, rear ports, power cable, and trays
response.reason: Witness identity (Sharp AR-9201) is settled and clear enough to price at worst case, but the seller's conflicting model claim and all condition/usage claims remain unverifiable remotely, so pricing must assume worst case until proof is supplied.
